conflicts: Price: Village Sewing lists the Moxie with 8 ft Loft at regular $5,995 (sale $4,495) and the Moxie with 10 ft Loft also at regular $5,995 (sale $5,095). Handi Quilter says the 10 ft length is an added 2 ft extension kit, so the two regular prices should differ. Catalog will use $5,995 as MSRP for the 8 ft bundle and flag the 10 ft price as [verify].

Speed: 1,800 spm max (dealers) vs 50 to 800 spm cruise speed range (manual excerpt, sewingmachinesplus.com PDF). These are different figures (mechanical max vs regulated cruise range), not a conflict, but both should be shown.

ownerThemes.theme: After a year an owner still calls it a brilliant small machine but notes tension changes take a moment to settle and that moving the head after stitching can snap the top thread and force a rethread.

Tension, thread breaking and fabric bunching are the recurring troubleshooting topics; the fix path is bobbin winding and threading checks first, and retiming by a Handi Quilter retailer if shredding persists.
Handi Quilter's own support pages treat tension and thread shredding as expected setup problems with a defined checklist, which suggests they are common enough to document.

Buyers deciding whether a 15 in frame longarm is worth roughly three times the price of a domestic straight stitch quilter
Similar all in spend: a dealer supported domestic quilting machine with BSR versus an entry longarm on a frame
The most common lower cost alternative for quilters who will keep quilting on a table rather than a frame

editorial.verdict: The Moxie is the lowest priced stand up longarm from a major brand that ships with stitch regulation and a frame in the box. The 15 in throat is the compromise: it is enough for pantographs and medium blocks, and it is the smallest frame longarm Handi Quilter sells.
editorial.whoFor: A home quilter with an 8 by 12 ft space who wants to quilt their own tops on a frame, wants regulated stitches from day one, and is not planning a quilting business.
editorial.skipIf: You want to quilt for others or do large custom work (look at 20 in and up), you have no room for a frame (sit down machines), or you only quilt lap size and smaller on a domestic.
editorial.keySpec: 15 in throat · 1,800 spm · 8 ft Loft frame included · stitch regulation built in
strengths: Stitch regulation (Precision and Cruise) is standard, not an add-on
Standard bundle includes an 8 ft Loft frame, so the sticker price is closer to the real price than machine only listings
M class bobbin and 134 needle system are the same consumables used across Handi Quilter's larger machines
weaknesses: 15 in throat is the smallest in Handi Quilter's frame lineup; usable quilting depth per pass will be less than 15 in once take up rollers and clamps are accounted for
Machine weight, throat height and Loft frame standalone price are not published on pages found
Tension and thread breakage dominate owner troubleshooting topics; retiming requires a dealer

checks.title: Confirm which frame is in the box
checks.body: Handi Quilter says the 8 ft Loft is standard and 10 ft is an extension kit. Some dealer pages list 8 ft and 10 ft bundles at the same regular price. Get the exact bundle in writing.

checks.title: Measure the room, not the frame
checks.body: Handi Quilter's own guidance is roughly 12 to 13 ft by 7.5 to 8 ft for a 10 ft frame. The 8 ft Loft needs about 2 ft of walking room on every side.

checks.title: Ask about Pro-Stitcher Lite compatibility
checks.body: Pro-Stitcher Lite is limited to the Moxie and Simply Sixteen on the Loft or Little Foot frames. If you might automate later, the frame choice now matters.

realCost.note: 8 ft Loft frame included at $5,995 MSRP; 2 ft extension to 10 ft is extra and its price was not published on pages found
